facts.raw_span: 5-year history of an asymptomatic, gradually enlarging, reddish hematomalike plaque
no previous history of trauma or any other systemic symptoms
nonindurated and well-defined 10 × 8-cm reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis
No local lymphadenopathy was observed
Vascular channel endothelial cells were positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
Negative for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and Wilms tumor 1 (WT1)
Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells
HIV: Negative
Hepatitis B: Negative
Hepatitis C: Negative
Poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation
Perls Prussian blue staining showed prominent hemosiderin deposits

concepts.why: The presence of vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40, along with the histologic findings of poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation, and the presence of hemosiderin deposits, are consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma, although the negative HHV-8 staining is unusual.

The clinical presentation of a reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis, along with the histologic findings of poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation, and the presence of hemosiderin deposits, are consistent with targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.

The presence of vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40, along with the histologic findings of poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation, could be consistent with angiosarcoma, although the low Ki-67 index and lack of cellular pleomorphism are not typical.

The patient's negative serologic tests for HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C, along with the histologic findings of poorly defined vascular proliferation and hemosiderin deposits, are consistent with a diagnosis of Hemosiderotic hemangioma.
